2607.03253.title: Semantic Segmentation-Driven Image-Level Diagnosis of Liver Cancers in Hematoxylin and Eosin Histopathology Images
2607.03253.paper_summary: As hematoxylin & eosin (H&E) staining constitutes the primary entry point in routine diagnostic workflows, computer-aided diagnosis from whole-slide H&E images is of particular clinical relevance. However, substantial variability in specimen preparation, staining protocols, and scanning conditions, together with inherent uncertainty in expert pixel-level annotations, makes automated analysis of H&E-stained images challenging. In this study, we propose a semantic segmentation-based framework for image-level diagnosis, grounded in the clinically motivated assumption that each histopathological image corresponds to a single cancer type. Image-level predictions are obtained by assigning the class of the dominant pixel-level label in the segmentation output. To ensure clinical relevance, we adopt the nnU-Net architecture and train it on a publicly available dataset collected in our study with pixel-level annotations for three liver cancer types: hepatocellular cacrcinoma (HCC; 55 images from 30 patients), cholangiocellular carcinoma (CCA; 55 images from 29 patients), and colorectal metastatic adenocarcinoma (CMA; 60 images from 30 patients). Annotations were independently provided by four pathologist. We hypothesize that the combination of stain normalization and semantic segmentation mitigates domain shift and reduces sensitivity to annotation noise. Five-fold cross-validation yielded balanced accuracy of 0.975 (HCC), 0.950 (CCA), and 1.000 (CMA), comparable to results obtained with immunohosthochemical staining and superior to several deep learning models trained on patch-level annotations. The proposed framework has the potential to support pathologists in prioritizing immunohistochemical marker selection, thereby reducing diagnostic costs and turnaround time. Integration with immunohistochemical findings improve overall diagnostic reliability.
2607.03253.paper_summary_zh: 由於蘇木精-伊紅（H&E）染色是常規診斷工作流程的主要切入點，因此基於全幻燈片H&E圖像的計算機輔助診斷具有特別的臨床相關性。<lb/>然而，樣本準備、染色方案和掃描條件的顯著變異，加上專家像素級標註的固有不確定性，使得H&E染色圖像的自動分析變得具有挑戰性。<lb/>在本研究中，我們提出了一種基於語義分割的框架，用於圖像級診斷，這一框架基於臨床驅動的假設，即每幅組織病理圖像對應於一種癌症類型。<lb/>圖像級預測是通過將分割輸出中佔主導地位的像素級標籤的類別分配給圖像來獲得的。<lb/>為了確保臨床相關性，我們採用了nnU-Net架構，並在我們研究中收集的公開數據集上進行訓練，該數據集包含三種肝癌類型的像素級標註：肝細胞癌（HCC；來自30名患者的55幅圖像）、膽管細胞癌（CCA；來自29名患者的55幅圖像）和結直腸轉移性腺癌（CMA；來自30名患者的60幅圖像）。<lb/>標註由四位病理學家獨立提供。我們假設染色標準化和語義分割的結合可以減輕領域轉移並降低對標註噪聲的敏感性。<lb/>五折交叉驗證的結果顯示，HCC的平衡準確率為0.975，CCA為0.950，CMA為1.000，這些結果與免疫組織化學染色的結果相當，並且優於幾個基於補丁級標註訓練的深度學習模型。<lb/>所提出的框架有潛力支持病理學家優先選擇免疫組織化學標記，從而降低診斷成本和周轉時間。<lb/>與免疫組織化學發現的整合提高了整體診斷的可靠性。
